itinerary.heading: Magiske Buenos Aires
itinerary.body:
Føl rytmen i Buenos Aires, og gjør deg klar for et skikkelig reiseeventyr

En overnatting i Buenos Aires er en perfekt måte å starte reisen til Antarktis på. Dette er hjemstedet til et stolt og mangfoldig samfunn av porteños, eller «folket fra havnen». Byen er en sanselig blanding av tidligere europeisk storhetstid og det fargesprakende latinamerikanske.  

Det er mange steder å utforske, blant annet mange parrillas som serverer nydelig autentisk argentinsk biff. Eller kanskje du vil vise frem danseferdighetene dine, her i den berømte tangoens hjemby.  

Hvorfor ikke komme noen dager før ekspedisjonen starter for å oppleve alt denne livlige byen har å by på? Eller bli med å utforske regionen på det valgfrie førprogrammet vårt.

itinerary.heading: Vi setter kurs sørover
itinerary.body:
Sett seil fra hovedstaden i Tierra del Fuego

Vi begynner dagen med et tidlig morgenfly til Ushuaia. Denne havnebyen er hovedstaden i den argentinske provinsen Tierra del Fuego, og den ligger mot et bakteppe av de praktfulle og mektige Andesfjellene. Ushuaia kjemper om tittelen som verdens sørligste by, og mange eventyr til Antarktis starter her, inkludert vårt.  

Du blir ønsket velkommen ombord på et hybriddrevet ekspedisjonsskip, spesielt konstruert for bærekraftig cruise i polare farvann. Etter en briefing med ekspedisjonsteamet, får du tid til å finne deg til rette på lugaren og utforske bekvemmelighetene og fasilitetene om bord. Eventyret ditt er endelig i gang!

itinerary.heading: Kryssing av Drakestredet
itinerary.body:
Kom i eventyrstemning og lær om naturen og vitenskapen i Antarktis

Under den to dager lange kryssingen gjennom Drakestredet, vil ekspedisjonsteamet fortelle deg alt du trenger å vite for å få mest mulig ut av det kommende eventyret. 

Besøk vitenskapssenteret om bord og få et innblikk om hva som venter deg. Lytt til eksperter som snakker engasjert om historien i Antarktis, vitenskapen under isen, og de alvorlige konsekvensene av vår tids miljøutfordringer. Du får vite hvordan du kan gjøre besøket ditt så trygt som mulig med minst mulig miljøpåvirkning, og du kan lære mer om folkeforskningsprogrammet om bord, som du også kan delta i for å bidra til å beskytte miljøet.  

Det er mer enn nok tid til å slappe av, så kos deg i spa- og velværeområdet, nyt deilig mat i restaurantene om bord, og møt andre reisende i Explorer Lounge & Bar.

itinerary.heading: Antarktis: en annen verden
itinerary.body:
Ekspedisjonen begynner, så gjør deg klar for alt den fantastiske Antarktishalvøya har å by på

Det er egentlig ingenting som kan forberede deg på dette. Stillhet og ro fyller sjelen din mens vi seiler gjennom det mørkeblå vannet, forbi mektige isbreer og isfjell på størrelse med katedraler. Hvert øyeblikk i Antarktis vil gjøre inntrykk på deg.  

Store grupper pingviner samler seg på isflakene for å unngå de listige leopardselene som jakter på dem, mens majestetiske hvaler glir forbi uberørte isfjell og sluker stimer av krill. Når du ser opp, kan du få øye på noen av de mange artene av antarktiske sjøfugler som holder til her, blant annet storjo, skarver, petreller og terner. 

Her er det naturen som hersker, og vi er bare tilskuere. Den erfarne kapteinen vår følger hele tiden med på forholdene for å lage den mest eventyrlige reiseruten for oss. Vi skal tilbringe ni innholdsrike dager med å utforske flere av de mange potensielle landingsstedene. Hver dag byr på noe nytt og spennende.  

Der de fleste Antarktis-ekspedisjoner tar slutt, vil din fortsette med økt intensitet, når vi reiser videre til noen av de mindre utforskede områdene. Husk, dette er et ekspedisjonscruise! Det betyr at vi kan tilpasse reiseruten vår etter sjø- og isforholdene. Vi vil forsøke å tilbringe minst én dag, om ikke flere, i hver av de følgende regionene: 

Sør-Shetlandsøyene: Sør-Shetlandsøyene er en øygruppe med et tyvetalls øyer og et dramatisk landskap, og som oftest er dette det første glimtet reisende ser av Antarktis. Øyene er ikke bare slående vakre, de er også fulle av dyreliv, og de byr på et levende og nært møte med naturens kraft og mangfold. 

Antarktissundet: En sjeldent besøkt perle i området. Antarktissundet fungerer som en mektig inngangsport til Weddellhavet, og er kjent for noen av de største platåformede isfjellene. Denne imponerende korridoren av is og vann er et viktig habitat for den sjeldne adeliepingvinen, og her kan du virkelig få et unikt innblikk i Antarktis' prakt og storhet. 

Gerlachestredet: 

Gerlachestredet er en viktig del av utforskningen av Antarktis. Her finner vi skjermede skipsleier som er ideelle for nære møter med noen av kontinentets mest kjente severdigheter. Dette er området der skipets navnebror, Roald Amundsen, i 1898 seilte om bord på Belgica før han og mannskapet ble de første til å overvintre i Antarktis. Området er ofte besøkt av knølhvaler og andre hvaler, og byr på 360-graders utsikt over snødekte alpine landskap, som er en virkelig imponerende bakgrunn for antarktiske eventyr. 

Penolastredet (sør for Lemairekanalen): 

Penolastredet, som nås via Den franske kanal, byr på en spektakulær labyrint av øyer fulle av pingviner, med massive, isdekte topper langs kysten. Dette avsidesliggende området er ofte utenfor rekkevidden til vanlige sjøreiser. Det kryr av dyreliv her, samtidig som det byr på ubegrensede muligheter for utforskning. Den store mengden havis gjør ikke bare området mer spektakulært, men øker også sjansene for å observere seler og annet dyreliv. Hvis is- og sjøforholdene tillater det, kan ekspedisjonsteamet velge den fantastiske Lemaire-kanalen i stedet for Penolastredet. Førstnevnte blir ofte hyllet som verdens mest pittoreske kanal, og det er ikke uten grunn.  

Om bord vil ekspedisjonsteamet fortsette med forelesningene sine, med fascinerende kunnskap om de mange underverkene på det frosne kontinentet.

itinerary.heading: Tilbake gjennom Drakestredet
itinerary.body:
Tenk tilbake på eventyret ditt

I dag setter skipet vårt kursen nordover igjen etter en spennende tid i Antarktis. Mens vi seiler gjennom Drakestredet tilbake til Ushuaia, får du mange muligheter til å nyte tiden til sjøs. 

Bli med ekspedisjonsteamet i vitenskapssenter for å lære mer om det som interesserer deg, og bidra i folkeforskningsprogrammet om bord. Få hjelp av ekspedisjonsteamet til å identifisere arter som er fanget på bildene dine.  

Slapp av med en behandling i spa- og velværeområdet, eller nyt den friske luften fra boblebadene på dekk. Avslutt kvelden i Explorer Lounge & Bar med de nye vennene du har fått på turen, og del opplevelser over en avslappende drink.

itinerary.heading: Ushuaia og Buenos Aires
itinerary.body:
Avslutt ekspedisjonen på herlig vis i Buenos Aires

Ekspedisjonscruiset ender der det startet, i Ushuaia, hovedstaden i Tierra del Fuego. Herfra tar vi fly tilbake til Buenos Aires. Men hvis du fortsatt er lysten på flere eventyr, trenger det ikke være et punktum for reisen.

Buenos Aires er en by rik på kultur, med fantastisk arkitektur og utsøkte spisesteder. Hvis du har lyst til å bli lenger, er du velkommen til å bli med på det valgfrie etterprogrammet vårt, før du reiser hjem igjen.

heading: Polarsirkel-ekspedisjon
intro: Cruise til Antarktis – Ekspedisjon til den sørlige polarsirkelen
sellingPoints: Bli med oss når vi forsøker å navigere gjennom havisen og krysse den antarktiske polarsirkelen – for å utforske det skjulte riket på det sjuende kontinentet.
Det mildere sommerværet betyr at vi kan prøve å seile sør for polarsirkelen til avsidesliggende og fantastiske Marguerite Bay.
Her får du sjansen til å se hvaler, unge pingviner, dra på fotturer, kajakkpadling, dra på iscruise og til og med campe i snøen i Antarktis.

itinerary.body:
Fly til Ushuaia og start eventyret ditt 

Eventyret ditt begynner med en tidlig morgenflyvning til Ushuaia, hvor du får se det hybriddrevne ekspedisjonsskipet, som er spesialdesignet for utforsking i polare farvann.

Denne travle havnen er hovedstaden i provinsen Tierra del Fuego i Argentina. Den mektige Martial-breen danner et fantastisk bakteppe for byen som også kjemper om tittelen som verdens sørligste by.

itinerary.heading: Gjør deg klar for Antarktis
itinerary.body:
Fokus på vitenskap og læring før det antarktiske eventyret 

Under den to dager lange kryssingen gjennom Drakestredet, utruster ekspedisjonsteamet deg med alt du trenger for å få mest mulig ut polarekspedisjonen. 

Besøk vitenskapssenteret om bord og få et innblikk om hva som venter deg. Lytt til eksperter som lidenskapelig forteller deg historien om Antarktis, vitenskapen under isen, og virkningen av klimaendringer og plastforurensning. Du lærer også hvordan du kan gjøre besøket ditt så trygt som mulig, og du får mer informasjon om folkeforskningsprogrammene du kan være med på.  

Det er mer enn nok tid til å slappe av, så kos deg i boblebadet og panoramabadstuen, nyt deilig mat og møt andre reisende i Explorer Lounge & Bar.

itinerary.heading: Antarktis: en annen verden
itinerary.body:
Opplev den majestetiske naturen i Antarktis 

Det er egentlig ingenting som kan forberede deg på dette. Det er umulig å være uberørt når du er omgitt av fantastiske isbreer og isfjell på størrelse med katedraler.  

Store grupper med pingviner flokker seg sammen på isflakene for å unngå leopardselene som jakter på dem. Majestetiske hvaler på vandring glir mellom imponerende isfjell, på jakt etter krillstimene de lever av. Fugleentusiaster bør rette blikket mot himmelen for å se noen av de mange artene av antarktiske sjøfugler som lever her, som rovmåker, skarver, stormfugler og terner. 

Her er det naturen som råder, og vi er her bare som observatører. Den erfarne kapteinen vår vil hele tiden sjekke forholdene for å planlegge den best mulige reiseruten for eventyret ditt. I løpet av elleve spennende dager får du utforske flere av de mange mulige landingsstedene. Du kan være trygg på at hver dag byr på noe nytt og spennende.  

Vi krysser den antarktiske polarsirkelen og fortsetter langt sør til Marguerite Bay, med utforskning av ulike øyer underveis. Når mulighetene byr seg, blir du med ekspedisjonsteamet på landstigninger og iscruise. Du får kanskje til og med sjansen til å dra ut blant isfjellene med kajakk. 

Tilbake om bord fortsetter ekspedisjonsteamet med forelesninger, som utvider forståelsen din av dette frosne kontinentet.

itinerary.heading: Tilbake gjennom Drakestredet
itinerary.body:
Tenk tilbake på eventyret ditt 

Etter ni dager med spennende utforsking, er ekspedisjonscruiset til vidunderne og dyrelivet i Antarktis snart over. Nyt tiden til sjøs mens vi vender tilbake til Ushuaia. 

Bli med ekspedisjonsteamet i vitenskapssenter for å lære mer om det som interesserer deg, og bidra i folkeforskningsprogrammet om bord. Få hjelp av ekspedisjonsteamet til å identifisere arter som er fanget på bildene dine. 

Slapp av med en behandling i spa- og velværeområdet, eller nyt den friske luften fra boblebadene på dekk. Avslutt kvelden i Explorer Lounge & Bar med de nye vennene du har fått på turen, og del opplevelser over en avslappende drink.

itinerary.heading: Ushuaia og Buenos Aires
itinerary.body:
Avslutt ekspedisjonen på herlig vis i Buenos Aires 

Ekspedisjonscruiset avsluttes når vi ankommer Ushuaia i Tierra del Fuego-provinsen, som er Argentinas sørligste. Herfra tar vi fly tilbake til Buenos Aires, men det trenger ikke være punktum for eventyret. 

Hvorfor ikke bli med på det valgfrie etterprogrammet vårt før du reiser hjem igjen?

itinerary.heading: Avreise fra Hamburg
itinerary.body:
Islandseventyret begynner

Ekspedisjonscruiset seiler fra Hamburg – en by full av historie, kunst og kultur. Det er mye å se og gjøre her, så ta deg litt tid til å utforske før du går om bord på ekspedisjonsskipet.  

Du vil se mange av byens store attraksjoner i gamlebyen, Altstadt, blant annet St. Nikolai-minnesmerket og den historiske gaten, Deichstraße. Gjør deg kjent med den interessante historien til to steder på UNESCOs verdensarvliste – Chilehaus og verdens største lagerbygningskompleks. 

Når du kommer om bord kan du hente en gratis ekspedisjonsjakke, møte ekspedisjonsteamet, utforske fasilitetene om bord og finne deg til rette i lugaren før vi kaster loss.

itinerary.heading: En dag til sjøs
itinerary.body:
Nyt en avslappet dag på sjøen om bord på MS Fridtjof Nansen

Mens ekspedisjonscruiset ditt tar deg fra Hamburg til Lysefjorden i Norge, får du muligheten til å lære mer om stedene du skal besøke sammen med ekspertene i ekspedisjonsteamet. Bli med på forelesninger i vitenskapssenteret, og få vite mer om reisen du har foran deg.

En dag på sjøen gir deg masse tid til å slappe av, og det moderne ekspedisjonsskipet vårt lar deg gjøre det med stil. Hvorfor ikke besøke velværeområdet, eller ta en tur i badstuen eller evighetsbassenget? Du vil garantert nyte de lekre, nordiske og internasjonale rettene våre, basert på lokale råvarer, som serveres i de tre restaurantene om bord.

itinerary.heading: Seiling i Lysefjorden
itinerary.body:
I dag skal vi seile inn i den 40 km lange Lysefjorden. Nyt en dag med fantastiske landskap fra observasjonsdekkene, og la deg imponere av den fantastiske utsikten til den lange og smale fjorden som ligger klemt mellom stupbratte fjellvegger.  

Fra fjorden kan vi ta en titt opp på Preikestolen, og holde utkikk etter den like berømte Kjeragbolten – en enorm kampestein som har kilt seg fast i en fjellsprekk. Er du klar for et eventyr kan du bli med ekspedisjonsteamet på en tur i en liten ekspedisjonsbåt eller kajakkpadling, og se den enorme fjorden fra et nytt perspektiv.

itinerary.heading: Shetlandsøyene
itinerary.body:
Utforsk den dype vikinghistorien på de skotske Shetlandsøyene

Vi seiler mot nordvest til Shetlandsøyene. Lerwick er hovedstaden her - en vennlig, viktoriansk-inspirert fiskerlandsby i et vakkert landskap. 

Ta deg en tur rundt i de smale gatene og finn små butikker som selger lokal whisky, ullgensere og karamell. I det gamle kaiområdet finner du Shetland-museet, hvor du blant annet kan se piktiske utskjæringer og blondesjal fra Shetland. Ikke langt unna finner du også Fort Charlotte og det majestetiske rådhuset. 

Ha kikkerten klar og se etter gråsel og vanlig sel langs strendene i Lerwick, samt lokalt fugleliv som smålom, rødstilk og storspove.

itinerary.heading: Tórshavn fra 900-tallet
itinerary.body:
Et besøk til Streymoy på Færøyene

Tórshavn ligger på Streymoy, som er den største øya i Færøyene. Tórshavn – «Tors havn» – ble grunnlagt av vikingene på 900-tallet, og er en av Nord-Europas eldste hovedsteder. 

Gå langs brosteinsbelagte smågater og se koselige, fargerike hus med torvtak. I de lokale museene kan du lære om byens opprinnelse, samt plantelivet, dyrelivet og geologien på Færøyene.  

Omtrent 800 m utenfor byen bruser Svartafossen over mosegrodde steiner. Og mens du vandrer langs sjøpromenaden kan du være på utkikk etter ærfugl, og den lett gjenkjennelige færøyske stæren med beige vingespisser.

itinerary.heading: Seyðisfjörðurs regnbue
itinerary.body:
Fosser og dyreliv i unike Seyðisfjörður

Innerst i en dyp fjord med mektige fjell og fosser, ligger det uvanlige tettstedet Seyðisfjörður. Fargerike trehus står på rekke og rad langs gatene, og Regnbuegaten er et fantastisk fotomotiv.  

Gå til den uvanlige lydskulpturen, Tvisongur, eller legg ut på en lengre fottur i åsene over byen. Du kan også besøke det private naturreservatet, Skalanes, hvor du kan se reinsdyr, polarrev og mink. Her kan du speide etter svarthalespove, heilo og jaktfalk, som er Europas største falk.

itinerary.heading: Lundefugl på Grímsey
itinerary.body:
Kryss den nordlige polarsirkel og se lundefugl

Grímsey er en avsidesliggende, forblåst øy med en fantastiske landskap, rikt dyreliv, myter og legender. Hvis været tillater det, går vi i land for å besøke lundefuglkoloniene.   

Siden Grímsey er den eneste delen av Island som ligger nord for den nordlige polarsirkel, får du også muligheten til å ta turen over til Arktis og tilbake! 

Innen 2050 vil Grímsey ligge utenfor polarsirkelen, siden grensen flytter seg nordover med omtrent 14 meter i året.

itinerary.heading: Akureyri og Goðafoss
itinerary.body:
Se fascinerende månelandskap og fossefall

Nyt synet av snødekte topper mens vi cruiser langs Eyjafjörður, som er Islands lengste fjord. Dette er et av Europas beste steder for å se knølhval, kvitnos og havnenise. Hold også utkikk etter spekkhogger, blåhval og finnhval.  

Islands «nordlige hovedstad», Akureyri, ligger innerst i fjorden. Nyt den fredfylte oasen i botanisk hage, og gled deg over en rekke førsteklasses spisesteder og museer.  

Et stykke unna kan du besøke den kjente Goðafoss, der turkis vann tordner ned mot sorte steiner. Du kan også holde utkikk etter ærfugl og harlekinender på innsjøen Mývatn, som er et av Islands mange områder med vulkansk aktivitet.

itinerary.heading: Nordvestregionen
itinerary.body:
Utforsk det nordvestlige Island i ekspedisjonsstil

Frihetsfølelsen er en av de beste tingene med ekspedisjonscruise. Vi planlegger å tilbringe dagen i den nordvestlige regionen av Island, men siden forholdene kan variere, har vi ikke noe konkret program. Men du kan være sikker på at kapteinen og ekspedisjonsteamet vi finne de beste mulighetene for eventyr denne dagen, basert på værforholdene.  

Kanskje tar vi en tur i de små ekspedisjonsbåtene våre, eller vi kan reise i land for en fottur, svømmetur eller strandrydding. Eller kanskje vi sjøsetter kajakkene. Hvis vi ser en gruppe hval mens vi seiler, kan det hende vi stopper for å se på dem. Vær klar for alt!

Ikke glem at du også kan delta på forelesninger om bord, besøke vitenskapssenteret, få tips fra den profesjonelle fotografen om bord eller ta en tur i badstuen.

itinerary.heading: Patreksfjörður og området rundt
itinerary.body:
En fantastisk strand, fosser og enestående forhold for fugletitting

I Patreksfjörður får du lære alt om fisketradisjonene i Europas vestligste tettsted. Herfra er det enkelt å reise til noen av de fantastiske landskapene og det mangfoldige dyrelivet som gjør dette avsidesliggende hjørnet av Island helt unikt. 

Utforsk området rundt på en fottur langs fjordene, eller se sel på stranden, Rauðasandur. Du kan også bli med på en tur til Dynjandi, hvor seks fosser samles til én. Sammen utgjør de det største og mest spektakulære fossefallet i Vestfjordene. Fugletittere bør ikke gå glipp av et besøk til Látrabjarg, hvor lundefugl, havsule, lomvi og alke klynger seg til Europas største fuglefjell. ching

itinerary.heading: Snæfellsnes-halvøya
itinerary.body:
Porten til spektakulære Snæfellsnes

Det er som om tiden har stått stille i det lille fiskeværet Stykkishólmur i Breiðafjörður-bukta, der fargerike hus står i kontrast til fjellene i horisonten.  

I nærheten finner du Snæfellsnes-halvøya nasjonalpark. Her ligger den fantastiske Snæfellsjökull-vulkanen med sin snøkalott på den vestre spissen på halvøya. Halvøya har fått kallenavnet «Lille Island» på grunn av de mange vulkanske landskapene. 

I nasjonalparken kan du besøke Djúpalónssandurs sorte sandstrender og basaltklippene, Lóndrangar. Du kan også kjøre snøskuter til toppen av isbreen Snæfellsjökull, eller bli med på en guidet kystvandring med besøk i en isbregrotte.

itinerary.heading: Heimaeys eksplosive fortid
itinerary.body:
Besøk en by som har overlevd et vulkanutbrudd

Heimaey ligger utenfor sørkysten av Island, og er den eneste bebodde øya i Vestmannaeyjar-øygruppen. Byen har en fascinerende historie, og du kan fortsatt se tydelige spor etter et kraftig vulkanutbrudd som nesten ødela øya.  

Besøk Eldheimar-museet hvor du kan finne et utgravd hjem som ligger frosset i tid, og lær mer om utbruddet og ettervirkningene av det. Eller hva med å ta en fottur for å se lundefugl på Stórhöfði. Ca. åtte millioner lundefugler hekker her hver sommer. Ta deg en klatretur i fjellet, Eldfell. På toppen av vulkanen får du fantastisk utsikt over byen nedenfor.

itinerary.heading: Reykjavík og videre
itinerary.body:
Opplev Reykjavík i ditt eget tempo

Selv om ekspedisjonscruiset til Island nærmer seg slutten, har du fortsatt et fantastisk reisemål igjen å utforske: Islands hovedstad Reykjavik, som er full av kunst, kultur og historie. 

Spaser langs byens hovedgate, Laugavegur, med butikker og gallerier, se den utrolige Hallgrímskirkja, og besøk Reykjavík kunstmuseum. Du kan også oppsøke en heittur pottur, direkte oversatt "en varm gryte". Det er et geotermisk basseng, som er en viktig del av kulturen på Island.

itinerary.heading: Your expedition begins
itinerary.body:
Explore British Columbia’s largest city

After an enjoyable breakfast at your hotel, we’ll take you on a city tour showcasing the main highlights of Vancouver.   

When the tour is over, you’ll be dropped at the pier where your expedition ship MS Roald Amundsen awaits you. Settle in and take your time to get to know the ship before listening to the safety briefing. 

Your knowledgeable Expedition Team will lead the way on excursions and landings. Get to know them and sit down to enjoy a welcome dinner — your adventure is now underway.

itinerary.heading: Canada's Inside Passage
itinerary.body:
Enjoy sublime scenery as we sail the Inside Passage 

The Inside Passage coastal route takes us through the great North American Pacific Fjordland, a protected stretch of water over 930 miles long. Unlike other cruises which pass through at night, you’ll be able to view the sublime scenery in all its glory during the day.   

Our smaller expedition ship allows us to reach areas that larger vessels can’t, meaning you’ll get to explore lesser-travelled channels with breathtaking scenery. Keep your cameras and binoculars at the ready to catch sight of whales, including humpback, fin, minke and perhaps even orcas.

itinerary.heading: Misty Fjords
itinerary.body:
Revel in a wilderness where wildlife thrives

Part of the Tongass National Forest, Misty Fjords is a pristine wilderness of evergreens, waterfalls and snowcapped peaks. The revered naturalist writer John Muir described the area as one of the most beautiful places he’d ever seen.  

Weather permitting, you'll join the Expedition Team to tour Misty Fjords in our small expedition boats or take kayaks out.

Misty Fjords is rich in wildlife. You’ll scan for mountain goats, black and brown bears and moose as you explore. The waters are home to Pacific salmon, otters, Steller sea lions, harbour seals, orcas and Dall’s porpoises. Skywards, you might spot herons and Bald Eagles.

itinerary.heading: Wrangell
itinerary.body:
Visit one of Alaska’s oldest harbour towns 

We continue cruising the Alaskan islands towards Wrangell. Only a mile out of town, Petroglyph Beach is where you'll see ancient rock carvings among the sand. 

Visit the local museum to learn more about Wrangell's fascinating past. Now part of the United States, it was once governed by Britain, Russia and the Łingít people. Cross to Shakes Island, where the Chief Shakes Tribal House and totem poles tell the story of the Indigenous Łingít people.  

Hikers will enjoy the nature trails, surrounded by alluring scenery at the mouth of Stikine River, and the foot of Mount Dewey at the edge of the rainforest.

itinerary.heading: Blended cultures of Sitka
itinerary.body:
Take in Sitka’s views and mix of cultures

Surrounded by Tongass National Forest, Sitka is only accessible by sea or air. Get out on deck for stunning views of the Sisters Mountains and Mount Edgecumbe volcano.  

Inhabited by the  Łingít people for 10,000 years, the town was settled by Russian explorers around the turn of the 19th century before being sold to the United States after Russia lost the Crimean War. Today, Sitka has roots in all three cultures.  

A visit to the Russian Orthodox cathedral and Russian Bishop's House is recommended. Admire ornate Haida and  Łingít totem poles at Sitka National Historical Park and enjoy a walking trail through the forest to the ocean.

itinerary.heading: Icy Strait expedition day
itinerary.body:
Embrace the thrill of wild Alaska

Today is another day of exploration as we sail into Icy Strait and take a closer look at some of the islands. Possible destinations to explore include George Island, Inian Islands and Idaho Inlet but – as ever – we will gauge the weather conditions and wildlife spotting opportunities to decide upon the best location. 

Using our expedition boats, we may get close to some of the rocky shores here, with the possibility of a landing and nature walk. The coast in this region grows more rugged the closer we get to the open sea, with rocky pinnacles and sea caves galore. Keep an eye out for whales, as well as sea lions, orcas and Bald Eagles.

itinerary.heading: Icy Bay
itinerary.body:
Spot wildlife in these glacier-fed waters

Today is an exploration day in Icy Bay. Three glaciers – Guyot, Yahtse and Tyndall – regularly calve into this bay. If conditions allow, you’ll explore in our small expedition boats or by kayak, immersing you in the remarkable beauty of this icy landscape.  

Wildlife abounds in the Gulf of Alaska, offering unrivalled photography opportunities. Humpback whales, orcas, Stellar sea lions, sea otters and harbour seals lazing on floating chunks of ice are often seen in these waters.

itinerary.heading: Across the Gulf of Alaska
itinerary.body:
A day of relaxation and birdwatching at sea

Your cruise continues across the Gulf of Alaska. It's the ideal time to enjoy onboard facilities such as the infinity pool, hot tubs, and sauna. Go for a run, hit the gym, or enjoy a massage in the spa.  

In the Science Centre, the Expedition Team invite you to join lectures about subjects such as Alaska’s wildlife, geology, glaciology, history and culture.  

Relax in the Explorer Lounge & Bar and share a drink with your fellow guests, or just sit back and enjoy the view. See if you can spot all three species of North Pacific albatross. The Laysan and Black-footed Albatross are often sighted, but the Short-tailed Albatross is harder to spot.

itinerary.heading: Kodiak's brown bears
itinerary.body:
Explore the home of the Alutiiq people

Kodiak Island got its nickname the ‘Emerald Isle’, due to its Spruce forests and grasslands, and it's the second-largest island in the US. 

The island’s most famous inhabitants are Kodiak brown bears. Around 3,500 of them live in the Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge, which covers two-thirds of the island.  

We’ll search for these powerful creatures in their natural habitat, marvelling at their size and grace from the safety of our small expedition boat. This perspective offers a rare glimpse into the lives of these bears against the backdrop of Alaska’s breathtakingly rugged landscape.

itinerary.heading: Brown bears in Katmai
itinerary.body:
Spot brown bears in Katmai National Park

Your adventure continues in the four million–acre Katmai National Park, which has over a dozen active volcanoes. Katmai is also home to more than 2,000 protected brown bears – the largest concentration in the world.  

Accompanied by an experienced bear guard, we'll be safely scouting for them from the deck or in our small expedition boats. They might be foraging for berries, digging for clams or catching fish in the stream. 

Depending on conditions, we might visit either Geographic Harbor, Kinak Bay or Kukak Bay.

itinerary.heading: Alaska Peninsula
itinerary.body:
Explore rugged scenery in an untamed wilderness

The Alaska Peninsula is an untamed wilderness and a haven for wildlife. The region is characterised by its raw coastal landscapes, towering mountains and secluded bays.  

Join your Expedition Team for close exploration of hidden bays and inlets along the shoreline, offering the opportunity to scout for bears, Bald Eagles, and marine species like sea otters and humpback whales. Learn about the geological evolution of the region, appreciating how natural forces have sculpted the unique topography around you.

itinerary.heading: Unga
itinerary.body:
Experience a deserted Alaskan town

Wild and deserted, Unga Village is an abandoned yet picturesque settlement on the southern end of Unga Island.  

It was settled by Unangax̂ in 1833 but was abandoned in 1969 as subsistence fishing proved insufficient to support living here. Today, the few wooden buildings that remain are the only evidence that people once lived here.  

A carpet of pink lousewort, fireweed and other wildflowers surrounds the abandoned shacks as nature has gradually taken over. Experience the eerie beauty of this place during a nature landing with our small expedition boats.

itinerary.heading: Discover Dutch Harbor
itinerary.body:
Learn the fascinating history of America’s biggest fishing port

America's largest fishing port, Dutch Harbor is a fascinating place to visit. As we sail towards it you may see Mount Makushin, a sometimes-steaming volcano reaching almost 6,000 ft.  

Here, you’ll learn about the local Indigenous Unangan people at the Museum of the Aleutians. Visit the Russian Orthodox Cathedral or tour the WWII museum commemorating the battle that took place here in 1942.  

Scout for Bald Eagles and puffins. Foxes, lemmings and wild horses thrive on land and whales, sea lions and porpoises in the waters. Dutch Harbor is where the reality television series The Deadliest Catch was filmed, following crab fishermen at work under extreme conditions.

itinerary.heading: Learning and leisure
itinerary.body:
Relax and reflect as we cruise along the coast

Part of being on an expedition cruise is taking time to connect with the sights and sounds of the world around you. A day at sea lets you do just that. Sit back and take in the panoramic views from our Explorer Lounge & Bar, from the infinity pool or from the outdoor hot tubs.  

Keep scanning the shores, seas and skies for puffins, auklets, and murrelets, especially closer to the coast. If you’re lucky, you might glimpse the Red-legged Kittiwake, only found in this part of the world. 

You'll learn more about the region's geography, climate and birdlife from the Expedition Team in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: St Paul
itinerary.body:
Look out for wildlife on the largest Pribilof Island

The windswept island of St Paul is home to the largest Unangan community in the US, numbering around 480. You can visit the historical remains of barabaras here – traditional dwellings built half-underground to protect against the sea winds.  

St Paul is also designated an Important Bird Area, and around 300 species of migrating birds use it as a resting point. Scan for Horned and Tufted Puffins, the Pribilof Sandpiper and the rare Red-legged Kittiwake.  

On the shore, you may find northern fur seals waddling and playing – half the world's population of these charming animals live on these islands.

itinerary.heading: St Matthew
itinerary.body:
Experience this wild, remote and isolated island

Part of the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge, 200 miles from the nearest village, St Matthew Island is wild, remote and isolated. You'll see traces of abandoned buildings between black sand beaches and wildflower-dotted tundra. A few hardy souls have tried – and failed – to make a home here.  

Today, the only inhabitants are birds, including thousands of puffins, murres and cormorants. On our nature landing, if we’re lucky, we’ll see the rare McKay’s Bunting, which breeds almost exclusively here — and listen out for the sound of the singing vole, named after its unusual warning cry.

itinerary.heading: Bering Sea
itinerary.body:
Watch for wildlife and relax at sea

As we cruise the Bering Sea, you'll have Russia to the west and the United States to the east.  

Natural wonders abound here, so keep an eye out for humpback whales, and seabirds wheeling through the skies. 

This is your last full sea day, so relax and enjoy your time on board. The Expedition Team will recap the highlights of your Alaskan adventure, and you can continue your journey of discovery in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: Nome
itinerary.body:
Learn about Nome’s golden past

Prospectors first came to Nome in 1898, and people still hunt for gold here today. You'll see evidence of the Gold Rush all around, including abandoned dredges, turn-of-the-century steam engines and old railroad tracks, lending the town a unique atmosphere. 

Nome was the end point of three of Roald Amundsen's great polar expeditions, including an attempt by air to reach the North Pole in 1926.  

Naturally, Nome is a fitting place to bid farewell to our own MS Roald Amundsen, before flying back to Seattle, where you’ll enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.heading: Seattle
itinerary.body:
End your adventure in the Emerald City

Your Alaskan adventure comes to an end in Seattle. 

If you have time before your onward journey, why not head to the Seattle Aquarium to see sea otters and a giant Pacific octopus. Or for incredible views of Puget Sound and the surrounding mountains, take a stroll through the nine-acre Olympic Sculpture Park, admiring the work of renowned artists as you go.  

For a feast of the senses, visit the famous Pike Place Market. Operating for over a century, this lively farmer’s market boasts everything from buskers and bars to salmon-throwing fishmongers! 

If you have the time to go farther afield, we recommend booking a Post-Programme with us and discovering some of the region’s natural highlights.

itinerary.heading: Lisbon
itinerary.body:
Set out from this enchanting city

The Portuguese capital is rich in history and culture. Take a stroll through the classical districts of Baixa and Bairro Alto, Chiado, and Alfama, the old Islamic quarter, where there are remains of a Roman theatre and Moorish fortress. A bit outside the city centre, you can visit the beautiful UNESCO World Heritage sites of Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery before you set sail. 

MS Fram awaits you in the harbour. After being welcomed aboard, settle into your cabin and begin your adventure at sea.   

With so much to see in and around Lisbon, why not arrive early and join one of our optional Pre-Programmes.

itinerary.heading: Porto (Leixões)
itinerary.body:
Explore the UNESCO-listed historic centre of Porto

Our first stop is Leixões, Portugal. From here, you can see the lighthouse of Leça, the Boa Nova Chapel, and the beautiful beach of Praia Azul.    

You can take a shuttle bus to Porto – famed for its port wine and UNESCO-listed historic centre. An undulating city made for walking, you'll fall in love with the pastel houses, colourful tiled façades, street art, ornate churches and panoramic views across the Douro River.   

Here, you can stroll along the bustling promenade by the Ribeira docks, cross the Dom Luís I Bridge, snack on delicious petiscos, and enjoy wine tastings at the port cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia.

itinerary.heading: Galician highlights
itinerary.body:
See Galicia's heritage in Ferrol

As we enter the ria of Ferrol, admire the imposing forts of La Palma and San Felipe that sit on either side of the headland, protecting the city within.    

Ferrol is one of Spain’s best preserved 18th century port cities. While you’re here, criss-cross Barrio de la Magdalena's grid of streets and explore the city’s maritime museums. 

El Camino Inglés, one of the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage routes, starts in Ferrol.  You may also be able to join an excursion to Santiago de Compostela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important Christian sites in the world.

itinerary.heading: At sea
itinerary.body:
Relax at sea and prepare for the adventures ahead

As we say goodbye to the Iberian Peninsula, MS Fram follows in the wake of Roman and Medieval traders as she heads for the springtime splendour of northern Europe. 

This is the perfect opportunity to make the most of your ship’s onboard comforts. Relax in the hot tubs or panoramic sauna and unwind in our Explorer Lounge & Bar. Look out for dolphins out on deck or join your Expedition Team for a talk or workshop, and discover more in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: Spring in the Isles of Scilly
itinerary.body:
Enjoy crystal waters, sandy beaches and natural beauty

Just 30 miles off the tip of Cornwall are the Isles of Scilly. This enchanting archipelago is home to some exquisite small islands with crystal clear waters, pristine beaches and stunning natural beauty. We’ll anchor the ship here and head ashore aboard local boats.  

If conditions allow, we’ll split our time here. You can explore Tresco’s white sandy beaches and the spectacular 19th century Abbey Gardens, which will be awash with the vibrant colours of spring. We also hope to visit St Mary’s, the largest of the isles. Wander through the charming streets of Hugh Town or follow the coastal paths to discover dramatic seascapes and rocky coves. Perhaps you may also like to join a boat trip around the archipelago, scouting for seals and breeding seabirds.

itinerary.heading: The Channel Islands
itinerary.body:
Discover a hidden gem on the edge of Europe

Lying between France and mainland Britain, the Channel Islands are a captivating archipelago with intriguing history and a landscape of unspoilt beaches, coastal castles and lush countryside. 

If conditions allow, we’ll anchor off Guernsey, the ‘Island of Flowers’, and take our small expedition boats towards St Peter Port Harbour, passing the 13th century Castle Cornet which stands guard on the headland.  

We also plan to visit Alderney, where you’ll join your Expedition Team for a guided walk, seeking out vibrant wildflowers amid the spring birdsong.

itinerary.heading: Dover
itinerary.body:
Say farewell by the renowned white cliffs

The sight of the white cliffs of Dover signals the end of this spring expedition cruise.  

As we sail into Dover with the iconic cliffs coming into view, we’ll dock at the harbour, and then it’s time to say a fond farewell to MS Fram and to all those who have made your expedition cruise such a memorable experience.

itinerary.heading: Depart from Dover
itinerary.body:
Your adventure begins

Your expedition cruise starts in Dover. If you have time before boarding MS FRAM, take a walk along the famous white cliffs at St Margaret's Bay for incredible views of the coastline and the sparkling English Channel below. 

Once you've picked up your expedition jacket and settled into your cabin, you'll have a chance to meet your Expedition Team, who'll be your friendly hosts and knowledgeable guides. Then enjoy your first dinner aboard the ship – your adventure has begun.

itinerary.heading: Harlingen
itinerary.body:
Experience the Frisian port city of Harlingen

Harlingen lies on the shores of the Wadden Sea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it’s home to the last traditional pottery factory in the Netherlands. 

A city of canals and pretty harbours, you can explore on foot or by bike, and if conditions allow, we can take to the water to cruise the canals aboard our small expedition boats.  

You'll find traditional sailing ships and historic warehouses around the old harbours of Noorderhaven and Zuiderhaven. Don’t miss the Harlingen Aardewerkmuseum, where you can admire displays of distinctive Frisian pottery.

itinerary.heading: Heligoland
itinerary.body:
Discover the peaceful charm of this historic island

Just off the German mainland, tiny Heligoland was once a base for pirates and the strategic prize for a string of warring nations. Now this peaceful, traffic-free island is better known for its stunning nature, and at certain times of the year, its birdlife.  

If conditions allow, local boats will take us ashore to explore both of Heligoland’s distinctive islands. On one island, you can walk the scenic trails along the red cliffs to look out for nesting birdlife such as Northern Gannets and Common Guillemots. On the other, you can stroll along the fine white sands lined by dunes in search for seals lounging around the shores.

itinerary.heading: Hamburg
itinerary.body:
Explore UNESCO sites in Germany’s second city

We arrive in Hamburg, the second-largest city in Germany and one of the greenest urban areas in Europe.   

There’s much to see and do in Hamburg – sometimes called the 'Venice of the North' due to its picturesque canals between lake Alster and river Elbe. You’ll find many attractions in the old town district of Altstadt, like St Nikolai Memorial and the historic street of Deichstraße. Hamburg is also home to UNESCO World Heritage sites, including Chilehaus, and the world's largest historic warehouse complex in “Speicherstadt”. Join a tour or discover the city at your own pace.

itinerary.heading: Esbjerg
itinerary.body:
Get a taste of Denmark on the Jutland peninsula

The first stop on our journey to the Arctic is Esbjerg on the west coast of Denmark’s Jutland peninsula. As we approach, look out for the giant ‘Man Meets the Sea’ statues sitting by the shore.  

Esbjerg is a blend of historic charm and modern Scandinavian chic, and it’s easy to get around on foot. A shuttle bus will take you into the centre to explore at your leisure. Why not treat yourself to a typical smørrebrød for lunch. You’ll find Denmark’s famous open rye bread sandwiches irresistibly displayed in many bakery windows. 

After lunch, it’s time to say goodbye to Denmark as we set sail for Norway. Enjoy an afternoon at sea making the most of your ship’s facilities. Why not relax in the hot tubs or watch the world go by from the Explorer Lounge & Bar.

itinerary.heading: Haugesund
itinerary.body:
Step back in time at the homeland of Vikings kings 

As we reach Norway, we’ll head for the region of Haugesund. Known for its Viking connections, it was here that King Harald Fairhair first united Norway into a single kingdom. From this royal seat, Norway’s kings long controlled the renowned shipping route Nordvegen, or ‘the way to the north’, from which the country takes its name. 

Today, this Viking past lives on in the area’s many historic sites. If conditions allow, we'll visit a recreated Viking settlement on the small island of Bukkøya, and on nearby Karmøy, you can delve deeper into Norway’s Viking and maritime history at the Nordvegen History Centre.

itinerary.heading: Sognefjord
itinerary.body:
Discover how glaciers shaped the Norwegian landscape 

In the morning, we plan to cruise deep into Sognefjorden, the longest and deepest fjord in Norway, to the tiny hamlet of Fjærland. Only 300 people live in this idyllic village with its many charming old buildings and weaving traditions. This is also the place where Sognefjorden meets Jostedalsbreen, the largest glacier on the European continent. 

A visit to the Norwegian Glacier Museum is the included activity of the day. There you can learn why glacier ice is blue and how the fjords were formed. You can even perform a few experiments with 1,000-year-old glacier ice and watch a panoramic film about Europe’s largest glacier.

itinerary.heading: Åndalsnes
itinerary.body:
Soak up breathtaking panoramas in this fjordside town 

Nestled at the end of the Romsdalsfjord, Åndalsnes is surrounded by soaring mountains, deep valleys and dramatic fjords. The scenery around this alpine town is simply awe-inspiring. 

 

To take it all in, hop on the gondola from the town centre for the five-minute scenic journey up Mount Nesaksla, some 2,300 ft above sea level. Here you can revel in 360-degree views of the town and the towering mountains of Romsdalshorn and Venjetinden beyond. 

To truly immerse yourself in this incredible landscape, join us for an exhilarating hike or, if conditions allow, you can enjoy a peaceful kayak paddle in the fjord.

itinerary.heading: Toward the Arctic Circle
itinerary.body:
Along the Helgeland coast to Arctic Norway

As we sail towards the wild beauty of the Lofoten archipelago, enjoy a day at sea. 

Continue your discovery on board with your Expedition Team by joining a talk or workshop and deepen your understanding with a visit to the Science Centre. Relax in the panoramic Explorer Lounge & Bar, and as we pass Helgeland, watch for the silhouette of the Seven Sisters mountain range. This impressive coastal range is home to the Torghatten mountain, recognisable by its distinctive hole through the middle. 

Later in the day, we’ll cross the Arctic Circle as we venture further north and into the Arctic.

itinerary.heading: Lofoten
itinerary.body:
Experience dramatic panoramas

Approaching the dramatically steep mountains of Lofoten by ship is an experience that’s unforgettable. You’ll be in awe of the landscapes as we sail towards this region of windswept islands, sheltered bays, and some of the most beautiful fjords in the world. Look out for Sea Eagles as you admire the exceptional beauty of this stretch of coastline.

Today we aim to explore the famed Lofoten Islands from the fishing port of Svolvaer. Learn how the rugged landscapes and a history of fishing have influenced life in Lofoten or explore the soul-stirring landscape up close on a hike with your Expedition Team.

itinerary.heading: Tromsø
itinerary.body:
Follow in the footsteps of polar explorers at the gateway to the Arctic

Set in a majestic landscape, this small, cosmopolitan city has an exciting past and plenty of fascinating sights to discover. 

It was the base for many a historic Arctic expedition, including those of Roald Amundsen, and its situation 250 miles north of the Polar Circle has led to it being called the ‘Gateway to the Arctic’. At the Polar Museum, discover the city’s exploration heritage, and see the Arctic Cathedral – with its huge stained-glass window, it’s one of the most striking landmarks in Tromsø. You can also take the Fjellheisen cable car to the top of Storsteinen for incredible views.

itinerary.heading: The North Cape
itinerary.body:
Discover majestic Arctic landscapes at Europe’s northernmost point

The captivating North Cape marks mainland Europe’s northernmost point. This rugged promontory on the north of Magerøya island truly feels like the end of the Earth. 

Here, we’ll venture across the wild Arctic landscape towards the cape’s towering cliff edge, which sits around a thousand feet above the Barents Sea. Feel a sense of awe as you drink in the panoramas, and as you gaze towards the horizon, think of the adventures yet to come as your voyage heads even further north.  

Discover more about the history of this remarkable site at the North Cape Hall.

itinerary.heading: Enjoy a day at sea
itinerary.body:
A peaceful interlude in your adventure

Spend the day at your leisure as we sail across the Barents Sea deeper into the Arctic towards the Svalbard archipelago. Savour the quiet moments, simply appreciating the peaceful feeling of being at sea. This is a rare opportunity to disconnect and get a break from the modern world.

Feeling active? You can enjoy a workout in the gym or simply relax in the panoramic sauna while gazing out at the view. As ever, our Expedition Team will be on hand to answer any questions you may have and offer insights about these Arctic islands.

itinerary.heading: Scenic Spitsbergen
itinerary.body:
A land of spectacular beauty

Svalbard’s largest island Spitsbergen showcases Arctic beauty in its untouched glory; a wilderness of steep mountains, stark glaciers and eerily beautiful islands. Over the next three days you’ll visit some of the world’s most dramatic fjords and see glaciers preparing to calve icebergs into the sea.  

Each day will be different. From landings to kayaking, be ready for anything as your Captain and Expedition Team decide on the best landing sites and activities based on the day’s conditions. Perhaps we’ll head to the snowcapped peaks of Hornsund, or visit Ny-Ålesund, the starting point for Roald Amundsen’s expeditions north with the airship ‘Norge’. Now a hub for global science and climate research, you can still see remnants of the town’s history. 

If we’re lucky, we might even see the elusive polar bear in its natural environment, so keep your binoculars close at hand.

itinerary.heading: Longyearbyen
itinerary.body:
A final day on top of the world

Your Norway and Svalbard adventure draws to a close in Longyearbyen. A transfer will take you to the airport for your flight home. You'll return with a wealth of knowledge about Arctic animals, geology, history, polar ice and climate change – and memories of an incredible experience that will last a lifetime. 

If you’re not ready to say goodbye just yet, why not spend some more time in the Arctic and join our optional Post-Programme.

itinerary.heading: Hamburg
itinerary.body:
Your adventure begins

Your expedition cruise to Norway and Svalbard begins in Hamburg – a city full of history, art and culture. There's plenty to see and do here, so take some time to explore before boarding your expedition ship. 

You'll discover many of the city's attractions in the old town district, ‘Altstadt’, including St Nikolai Memorial and the historic street of Deichstraße. Why not discover the interesting history of two UNESCO World Heritage sites – Chilehaus and the world's largest warehouse complex. 

Once aboard, you'll collect your complimentary expedition jacket, meet your Expedition Team, explore the onboard comforts of your ship and settle into your cabin as we set sail.

itinerary.heading: Esbjerg
itinerary.body:
Get a taste of Denmark on the Jutland peninsula

The first stop on our journey to the Arctic is Esbjerg on the west coast of Denmark’s Jutland peninsula. As we approach, look out for the giant ‘Man Meets the Sea’ statues sitting by the shore. 

Esbjerg is a blend of historic charm and modern Scandinavian chic, and it’s easy to get around on foot. A shuttle bus will take you into the centre to explore at your leisure. Why not treat yourself to a typical smørrebrød for lunch. You’ll find Denmark’s famous open rye bread sandwiches irresistibly displayed in many bakery windows. 

After lunch, it’s time to say goodbye to Denmark as we set sail for Norway. Enjoy an afternoon at sea making the most of your ship’s facilities. Why not relax in the hot tubs or watch the world go by from the Explorer Lounge & Bar.

itinerary.heading: Haugesund
itinerary.body:
Step back in time at the homeland of Vikings kings

As we reach Norway, we’ll head for the region of Haugesund. Known for its Viking connections, it was here that King Harald Fairhair first united Norway into a single kingdom. From this royal seat, Norway’s kings long controlled the renowned shipping route Nordvegen, or ‘the way to the north’, from which the country takes its name. 

Today, this Viking past lives on in the area’s many historic sites. If conditions allow, we'll visit a recreated Viking settlement on the small island of Bukkøya, and on nearby Karmøy, you can delve deeper into Norway’s Viking and maritime history at the Nordvegen History Centre.

itinerary.heading: Sognefjord
itinerary.body:
Discover how glaciers shaped the Norwegian landscape

In the morning, we plan to cruise deep into Sognefjorden, the longest and deepest fjord in Norway, to the tiny hamlet of Fjærland. Only 300 people live in this idyllic village with its many charming old buildings and weaving traditions. This is also the place where Sognefjorden meets Jostedalsbreen, the largest glacier on the European continent. 

A visit to the Norwegian Glacier Museum is the included activity of the day. There you can learn why glacier ice is blue and how the fjords were formed. You can even perform a few experiments with 1,000-year-old glacier ice and watch a panoramic film about Europe’s largest glacier.

itinerary.heading: Åndalsnes
itinerary.body:
Soak up breathtaking panoramas in this fjordside town 

Nestled at the end of the Romsdalsfjord, Åndalsnes is surrounded by soaring mountains, deep valleys and dramatic fjords. The scenery around this alpine town is simply awe-inspiring. 

To take it all in, hop on the gondola from the town centre for the five-minute scenic journey up Mount Nesaksla, some 2,300 ft above sea level. Here you can revel in 360-degree views of the town and the towering mountains of Romsdalshorn and Venjetinden beyond. 

To truly immerse yourself in this incredible landscape, join us for an exhilarating hike or, if conditions allow, you can enjoy a peaceful kayak paddle in the fjord.

itinerary.heading: Toward the Arctic Circle
itinerary.body:
Along the Helgeland coast to Arctic Norway

As we sail towards the wild beauty of the Lofoten archipelago, enjoy a day at sea. 

Continue your discovery on board with your Expedition Team by joining a talk or workshop and deepen your understanding with a visit to the Science Centre. Relax in the panoramic Explorer Lounge & Bar, and as we pass Helgeland, watch for the silhouette of the Seven Sisters mountain range. This impressive coastal range is home to the Torghatten mountain, recognisable by its distinctive hole through the middle. 

Later in the day, we’ll cross the Arctic Circle as we venture further north and into the Arctic.

itinerary.heading: Lofoten
itinerary.body:
Experience dramatic panoramas

Approaching the dramatically steep mountains of Lofoten by ship is an experience that’s unforgettable. You’ll be in awe of the landscapes as we sail towards this region of windswept islands, sheltered bays, and some of the most beautiful fjords in the world. Look out for Sea Eagles as you admire the exceptional beauty of this stretch of coastline.

Today we aim to explore the famed Lofoten Islands from the fishing port of Svolvaer. Learn how the rugged landscapes and a history of fishing have influenced life in Lofoten or explore the soul-stirring landscape up close on a hike with your Expedition Team.

itinerary.heading: Tromsø
itinerary.body:
Follow in the footsteps of polar explorers at the gateway to the Arctic

Set in a majestic landscape, this small, cosmopolitan city has an exciting past and plenty of fascinating sights to discover.

It was the base for many a historic Arctic expedition, including those of Roald Amundsen, and its situation 250 miles north of the Polar Circle has led to it being called the ‘Gateway to the Arctic’. At the Polar Museum, discover the city’s exploration heritage, and see the Arctic Cathedral – with its huge stained-glass window, it’s one of the most striking landmarks in Tromsø. You can also take the Fjellheisen cable car to the top of Storsteinen for incredible views.

itinerary.heading: Nordkapp
itinerary.body:
Oppdag majestetiske arktiske landskap på Europas nordligste punkt

Vakre Nordkapp er det europeiske fastlandets nordligste punkt. Når man står på denne kuperte odden på nordsiden av Magerøya, føler man virkelig at man er ved verdens ende. 

Her reiser vi over det ville arktiske landskapet mot Nordkapps ruvende klippekant, som ligger omtrent 300 meter over Barentshavet. Opplev en følelse av ærefrykt mens du opplever panoramautsikten og ser mot horisonten, der eventyrene som ligger foran deg, venter på reisen videre nordover.  

Oppdag mer om historien til dette utrolige stedet på Nordkapphallen.

itinerary.heading: Enjoy a day at sea
itinerary.body:
A peaceful interlude in your adventure

Spend the day at your leisure as we sail across the Barents Sea deeper into the Arctic towards the Svalbard archipelago. Savour the quiet moments, simply appreciating the peaceful feeling of being at sea. This is a rare opportunity to disconnect and get a break from the modern world. 

Feeling active? You can enjoy a workout in the gym or simply relax in the panoramic sauna while gazing out at the view. As ever, our Expedition Team will be on hand to answer any questions you may have and offer insights about these Arctic islands.

itinerary.heading: Scenic Spitsbergen
itinerary.body:
A land of spectacular beauty

Svalbard’s largest island Spitsbergen showcases Arctic beauty in its untouched glory; a wilderness of steep mountains, stark glaciers and eerily beautiful islands. Over the next three days you’ll visit some of the world’s most dramatic fjords and see glaciers preparing to calve icebergs into the sea.  

Each day will be different. From landings to kayaking, be ready for anything as your Captain and Expedition Team decide on the best landing sites and activities based on the day’s conditions. Perhaps we’ll head to the snowcapped peaks of Hornsund, or visit Ny-Ålesund, the starting point for Roald Amundsen’s expeditions north with the airship ‘Norge’. Now a hub for global science and climate research, you can still see remnants of the town’s history. 

If we’re lucky, we might even see the elusive polar bear in its natural environment, so keep your binoculars close at hand.

itinerary.heading: Longyearbyen
itinerary.body:
A final day on top of the world

Your Norway and Svalbard adventure draws to a close in Longyearbyen. A transfer will take you to the airport for your flight home. You'll return with a wealth of knowledge about Arctic animals, geology, history, polar ice and climate change – and memories of an incredible experience that will last a lifetime. 

If you’re not ready to say goodbye just yet, why not spend some more time in the Arctic and join our optional Post-Programme.

itinerary.heading: Lisbon
itinerary.body:
Set out from this enchanting city

The Portuguese capital is rich in history and culture. Take a stroll through the classical districts of Baixa and Bairro Alto, Chiado, and Alfama, the old Islamic quarter, where there are remains of a Roman theatre and Moorish fortress. A bit outside the city centre, you can visit the beautiful UNESCO World Heritage sites of Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery before you set sail. 

MS Fram awaits you in the harbour. After being welcomed aboard, settle into your cabin and begin your adventure at sea.   

With so much to see in and around Lisbon, why not arrive early and join one of our optional Pre-Programmes.

itinerary.heading: Porto (Leixões)
itinerary.body:
Explore the UNESCO-listed historic centre of Porto 

Our first stop is Leixões, Portugal. From here, you can see the lighthouse of Leça, the Boa Nova Chapel, and the beautiful beach of Praia Azul.  

You can take a shuttle bus to Porto – famed for its port wine and UNESCO-listed historic centre. An undulating city made for walking, you'll fall in love with the pastel houses, colourful tiled façades, street art, ornate churches and panoramic views across the Douro River.

Here, you can stroll along the bustling promenade by the Ribeira docks, cross the Dom Luís I Bridge, snack on delicious petiscos, and enjoy wine tastings at the port cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia.

itinerary.heading: Galician highlights
itinerary.body:
See Galicia's heritage in Ferrol

As we enter the ria of Ferrol, admire the imposing forts of La Palma and San Felipe that sit on either side of the headland, protecting the city within. 

Ferrol is one of Spain’s best preserved 18th century port cities. While you’re here, criss-cross Barrio de la Magdalena's grid of streets and explore the city’s maritime museums. 

El Camino Inglés, one of the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage routes, starts in Ferrol.  You may also be able to join an excursion to Santiago de Compostela, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important Christian sites in the world.

itinerary.heading: At sea
itinerary.body:
Relax at sea and prepare for the adventures ahead

As we say goodbye to the Iberian Peninsula, MS Fram follows in the wake of Roman and Medieval traders as she heads for the springtime splendour of northern Europe.   

This is the perfect opportunity to make the most of your ship’s onboard comforts. Relax in the hot tubs or panoramic sauna and unwind in our Explorer Lounge & Bar. Look out for dolphins out on deck or join your Expedition Team for a talk or workshop, and discover more in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: Spring in the Isles of Scilly
itinerary.body:
Enjoy crystal waters, sandy beaches and natural beauty

Just 30 miles off the tip of Cornwall are the Isles of Scilly. This enchanting archipelago is home to some exquisite small islands with crystal clear waters, pristine beaches and stunning natural beauty. We’ll anchor the ship here and head ashore aboard local boats. 

If conditions allow, we’ll split our time here. You can explore Tresco’s white sandy beaches and the spectacular 19th-century Abbey Gardens, which will be awash with the vibrant colours of spring. We also hope to visit St Mary’s, the largest of the isles. Wander through the charming streets of Hugh Town or follow the coastal paths to discover dramatic seascapes and rocky coves. Perhaps you may also like to join a boat trip around the archipelago, scouting for seals and breeding seabirds.

itinerary.heading: The Channel Islands
itinerary.body:
Discover a hidden gem on the edge of Europe

Lying between France and mainland Britain, the Channel Islands are a captivating archipelago with intriguing history and a landscape of unspoilt beaches, coastal castles and lush countryside.

If conditions allow, we’ll anchor off Guernsey, the ‘Island of Flowers’, and take our small expedition boats towards St Peter Port Harbour, passing the 13th century Castle Cornet which stands guard on the headland. 

We also plan to visit Alderney, where you’ll join your Expedition Team for a guided walk, seeking out vibrant wildflowers amid the spring birdsong.

itinerary.heading: Dover
itinerary.body:
See Britain’s dramatic coastline and the renowned white cliffs

As we approach mainland Britain, keep watch as the iconic White Cliffs of Dover appear on the horizon. 

When we arrive, why not take a walk along the famous white cliffs at St Margaret's Bay for incredible views of the coastline and the sparkling English Channel below. Or you can join your Expedition Team on a hike and see the imposing 11th-century Dover Castle. 

Dover is also a gateway to the UNESCO-listed Canterbury Cathedral, a medieval masterpiece echoing with the footsteps of pilgrims past and present.

itinerary.heading: Harlingen's rich heritage
itinerary.body:
Get to know the Frisian port city of Harlingen

Harlingen lies on the shores of the Wadden Sea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it’s home to the last traditional pottery factory in the Netherlands.   

A city of canals and pretty harbours, you can explore on foot or by bike, and if conditions allow, we can take to the water to cruise the canals aboard our small expedition boats.  

You'll find traditional sailing ships and historic warehouses around the old harbours of Noorderhaven and Zuiderhaven. Don’t miss the Harlingen Aardewerkmuseum, where you can admire displays of distinctive Frisian pottery.

itinerary.heading: Heligoland
itinerary.body:
Discover the peaceful charm of this historic island

Just off the German mainland, tiny Heligoland was once a base for pirates and the strategic prize for a string of warring nations. Now this peaceful, traffic-free island is better known for its stunning nature, and at certain times of the year, its birdlife. 

If conditions allow, local boats will take us ashore to explore both of Heligoland’s distinctive islands. On one island, you can walk the scenic trails along the red cliffs to look out for nesting birdlife such as Northern Gannets and Common Guillemots. On the other, you can stroll along the fine white sands lined by dunes in search for seals lounging around the shores.

itinerary.heading: Hamburg
itinerary.body:
End your cruise in Germany’s second city

 Your expedition cruise comes to an end as we arrive in Hamburg, the second-largest city in Germany and one of the greenest urban areas in Europe. 

There’s much to see and do in Hamburg. If you have time, you'll find many attractions in the old town district of Altstadt, including the St Nikolai Memorial and the historic street of Deichstraße. 

Hamburg is also home to UNESCO World Heritage sites, including Chilehaus, and the world's largest historic warehouse complex in Speicherstadt. Art lovers should head to Kunsthalle, the nation’s foremost art museum.

itinerary.heading: Vancouver
itinerary.body:
Arrive in Vancouver

Your expedition cruise starts with an overnight stay in Vancouver, a bustling and beautiful seaport city set against steep mountains. 

Vancouver's various neighbourhoods buzz with world-class farm-to-table cuisine. Don’t miss Gastown, Vancouver’s Victorian quarter. Here you'll find the 553-foot Vancouver Lookout, which offers a perfect 360-degree panoramic view over the city.

itinerary.heading: Your expedition begins
itinerary.body:
Explore British Columbia’s largest city

After an enjoyable breakfast at your hotel, we’ll take you on a city tour showcasing the main highlights of Vancouver.   

When the tour is over, you’ll be dropped at the pier where your expedition ship MS Roald Amundsen awaits you. Settle in and take your time to get to know the ship before listening to the safety briefing. 

Your knowledgeable Expedition Team will lead the way on excursions and landings. Get to know them and sit down to enjoy a welcome dinner — your adventure is now underway.

itinerary.heading: Canada's Inside Passage
itinerary.body:
Enjoy sublime scenery as we sail the Inside Passage 

The Inside Passage coastal route takes us through the great North American Pacific Fjordland, a protected stretch of water over 930 miles long. Unlike other cruises which pass through at night, you’ll be able to view the sublime scenery in all its glory during the day.   

Our smaller expedition ship allows us to reach areas that larger vessels can’t, meaning you’ll get to explore lesser-travelled channels with breathtaking scenery. Keep your cameras and binoculars at the ready to catch sight of whales, including humpback, fin, minke and perhaps even orcas.

itinerary.heading: Misty Fjords
itinerary.body:
Revel in a wilderness where wildlife thrives

Part of the Tongass National Forest, Misty Fjords is a pristine wilderness of evergreens, waterfalls and snowcapped peaks. The revered naturalist writer John Muir described the area as one of the most beautiful places he’d ever seen.  

Weather permitting, you'll join the Expedition Team to tour Misty Fjords in our small expedition boats or take kayaks out.

Misty Fjords is rich in wildlife. You’ll scan for mountain goats, black and brown bears and moose as you explore. The waters are home to Pacific salmon, otters, Steller sea lions, harbour seals, orcas and Dall’s porpoises. Skywards, you might spot herons and Bald Eagles.

itinerary.heading: Wrangell
itinerary.body:
Visit one of Alaska’s oldest harbour towns 

We continue cruising the Alaskan islands towards Wrangell. Only a mile out of town, Petroglyph Beach is where you'll see ancient rock carvings among the sand. 

Visit the local museum to learn more about Wrangell's fascinating past. Now part of the United States, it was once governed by Britain, Russia and the Łingít people. Cross to Shakes Island, where the Chief Shakes Tribal House and totem poles tell the story of the Indigenous Łingít people.  

Hikers will enjoy the nature trails, surrounded by alluring scenery at the mouth of Stikine River, and the foot of Mount Dewey at the edge of the rainforest.

itinerary.heading: Blended cultures of Sitka
itinerary.body:
Take in Sitka’s views and mix of cultures

Surrounded by Tongass National Forest, Sitka is only accessible by sea or air. Get out on deck for stunning views of the Sisters Mountains and Mount Edgecumbe volcano.  

Inhabited by the  Łingít people for 10,000 years, the town was settled by Russian explorers around the turn of the 19th century before being sold to the United States after Russia lost the Crimean War. Today, Sitka has roots in all three cultures.  

A visit to the Russian Orthodox cathedral and Russian Bishop's House is recommended. Admire ornate Haida and  Łingít totem poles at Sitka National Historical Park and enjoy a walking trail through the forest to the ocean.

itinerary.heading: Icy Strait expedition day
itinerary.body:
Embrace the thrill of wild Alaska

Today is another day of exploration as we sail into Icy Strait and take a closer look at some of the islands. Possible destinations to explore include George Island, Inian Islands and Idaho Inlet but – as ever – we will gauge the weather conditions and wildlife spotting opportunities to decide upon the best location. 

Using our expedition boats, we may get close to some of the rocky shores here, with the possibility of a landing and nature walk. The coast in this region grows more rugged the closer we get to the open sea, with rocky pinnacles and sea caves galore. Keep an eye out for whales, as well as sea lions, orcas and Bald Eagles.

itinerary.heading: Icy Bay
itinerary.body:
Spot wildlife in these glacier-fed waters

Today is an exploration day in Icy Bay. Three glaciers – Guyot, Yahtse and Tyndall – regularly calve into this bay. If conditions allow, you’ll explore in our small expedition boats or by kayak, immersing you in the remarkable beauty of this icy landscape.  

Wildlife abounds in the Gulf of Alaska, offering unrivalled photography opportunities. Humpback whales, orcas, Stellar sea lions, sea otters and harbour seals lazing on floating chunks of ice are often seen in these waters.

itinerary.heading: Across the Gulf of Alaska
itinerary.body:
A day of relaxation and birdwatching at sea

Your cruise continues across the Gulf of Alaska. It's the ideal time to enjoy onboard facilities such as the infinity pool, hot tubs, and sauna. Go for a run, hit the gym, or enjoy a massage in the spa.  

In the Science Centre, the Expedition Team invite you to join lectures about subjects such as Alaska’s wildlife, geology, glaciology, history and culture.  

Relax in the Explorer Lounge & Bar and share a drink with your fellow guests, or just sit back and enjoy the view. See if you can spot all three species of North Pacific albatross. The Laysan and Black-footed Albatross are often sighted, but the Short-tailed Albatross is harder to spot.

itinerary.heading: Kodiak's brown bears
itinerary.body:
Explore the home of the Alutiiq people

Kodiak Island got its nickname the ‘Emerald Isle’, due to its Spruce forests and grasslands, and it's the second-largest island in the US. 

The island’s most famous inhabitants are Kodiak brown bears. Around 3,500 of them live in the Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge, which covers two-thirds of the island.  

We’ll search for these powerful creatures in their natural habitat, marvelling at their size and grace from the safety of our small expedition boat. This perspective offers a rare glimpse into the lives of these bears against the backdrop of Alaska’s breathtakingly rugged landscape.

itinerary.heading: Brown bears in Katmai
itinerary.body:
Spot brown bears in Katmai National Park

Your adventure continues in the four million–acre Katmai National Park, which has over a dozen active volcanoes. Katmai is also home to more than 2,000 protected brown bears – the largest concentration in the world.  

Accompanied by an experienced bear guard, we'll be safely scouting for them from the deck or in our small expedition boats. They might be foraging for berries, digging for clams or catching fish in the stream. 

Depending on conditions, we might visit either Geographic Harbor, Kinak Bay or Kukak Bay.

itinerary.heading: Alaska Peninsula
itinerary.body:
Explore rugged scenery in an untamed wilderness

The Alaska Peninsula is an untamed wilderness and a haven for wildlife. The region is characterised by its raw coastal landscapes, towering mountains and secluded bays.  

Join your Expedition Team for close exploration of hidden bays and inlets along the shoreline, offering the opportunity to scout for bears, Bald Eagles, and marine species like sea otters and humpback whales. Learn about the geological evolution of the region, appreciating how natural forces have sculpted the unique topography around you.

itinerary.heading: Unga
itinerary.body:
Experience a deserted Alaskan town

Wild and deserted, Unga Village is an abandoned yet picturesque settlement on the southern end of Unga Island.  

It was settled by Unangax̂ in 1833 but was abandoned in 1969 as subsistence fishing proved insufficient to support living here. Today, the few wooden buildings that remain are the only evidence that people once lived here.  

A carpet of pink lousewort, fireweed and other wildflowers surrounds the abandoned shacks as nature has gradually taken over. Experience the eerie beauty of this place during a nature landing with our small expedition boats.

itinerary.heading: Discover Dutch Harbor
itinerary.body:
Learn the fascinating history of America’s biggest fishing port

America's largest fishing port, Dutch Harbor is a fascinating place to visit. As we sail towards it you may see Mount Makushin, a sometimes-steaming volcano reaching almost 6,000 ft.  

Here, you’ll learn about the local Indigenous Unangan people at the Museum of the Aleutians. Visit the Russian Orthodox Cathedral or tour the WWII museum commemorating the battle that took place here in 1942.  

Scout for Bald Eagles and puffins. Foxes, lemmings and wild horses thrive on land and whales, sea lions and porpoises in the waters. Dutch Harbor is where the reality television series The Deadliest Catch was filmed, following crab fishermen at work under extreme conditions.

itinerary.heading: Learning and leisure
itinerary.body:
Relax and reflect as we cruise along the coast

Part of being on an expedition cruise is taking time to connect with the sights and sounds of the world around you. A day at sea lets you do just that. Sit back and take in the panoramic views from our Explorer Lounge & Bar, from the infinity pool or from the outdoor hot tubs.  

Keep scanning the shores, seas and skies for puffins, auklets, and murrelets, especially closer to the coast. If you’re lucky, you might glimpse the Red-legged Kittiwake, only found in this part of the world. 

You'll learn more about the region's geography, climate and birdlife from the Expedition Team in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: St Paul
itinerary.body:
Look out for wildlife on the largest Pribilof Island

The windswept island of St Paul is home to the largest Unangan community in the US, numbering around 480. You can visit the historical remains of barabaras here – traditional dwellings built half-underground to protect against the sea winds.  

St Paul is also designated an Important Bird Area, and around 300 species of migrating birds use it as a resting point. Scan for Horned and Tufted Puffins, the Pribilof Sandpiper and the rare Red-legged Kittiwake.  

On the shore, you may find northern fur seals waddling and playing – half the world's population of these charming animals live on these islands.

itinerary.heading: St Matthew
itinerary.body:
Experience this wild, remote and isolated island

Part of the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge, 200 miles from the nearest village, St Matthew Island is wild, remote and isolated. You'll see traces of abandoned buildings between black sand beaches and wildflower-dotted tundra. A few hardy souls have tried – and failed – to make a home here.  

Today, the only inhabitants are birds, including thousands of puffins, murres and cormorants. On our nature landing, if we’re lucky, we’ll see the rare McKay’s Bunting, which breeds almost exclusively here — and listen out for the sound of the singing vole, named after its unusual warning cry.

itinerary.heading: Bering Sea
itinerary.body:
Watch for wildlife and relax at sea

As we cruise the Bering Sea, you'll have Russia to the west and the United States to the east.  

Natural wonders abound here, so keep an eye out for humpback whales, and seabirds wheeling through the skies. 

This is your last full sea day, so relax and enjoy your time on board. The Expedition Team will recap the highlights of your Alaskan adventure, and you can continue your journey of discovery in the Science Centre.

itinerary.heading: Nome
itinerary.body:
Learn about Nome’s golden past

Prospectors first came to Nome in 1898, and people still hunt for gold here today. You'll see evidence of the Gold Rush all around, including abandoned dredges, turn-of-the-century steam engines and old railroad tracks, lending the town a unique atmosphere. 

Nome was the end point of three of Roald Amundsen's great polar expeditions, including an attempt by air to reach the North Pole in 1926.  

Naturally, Nome is a fitting place to bid farewell to our own MS Roald Amundsen, before flying back to Seattle, where you’ll enjoy an overnight stay.

itinerary.heading: Seattle
itinerary.body:
End your adventure in the Emerald City

Your Alaskan adventure comes to an end in Seattle. 

If you have time before your onward journey, why not head to the Seattle Aquarium to see sea otters and a giant Pacific octopus. Or for incredible views of Puget Sound and the surrounding mountains, take a stroll through the nine-acre Olympic Sculpture Park, admiring the work of renowned artists as you go.  

For a feast of the senses, visit the famous Pike Place Market. Operating for over a century, this lively farmer’s market boasts everything from buskers and bars to salmon-throwing fishmongers! 

If you have the time to go farther afield, we recommend booking a Post-Programme with us and discovering some of the region’s natural highlights.

heading: Vitenskap og ro til havs | Lisboa til Buenos Aires
notIncludedInfo:
